\section[el efectivo]{el efectivo — the cash}

\label{lesson:ES-C628-efectivo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to get into debt, then the Spanish for to invest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el efectivo}
\textbf{el efectivo} — \textquotedblleft{}the cash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
¿Paga en efectivo o con tarjeta?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Are you paying in cash or by card?}
\end{quote}

\emph{En efectivo} — in cash. As an adjective it means effective.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{efectivo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{effectivus} 'productive', built on \emph{effectus}, from \emph{efficere} 'to bring about' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el efectivo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el efectivo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el efectivo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to get into debt, then the Spanish for to invest, then say \emph{el efectivo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el efectivo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The cash\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la transferencia]{la transferencia — the bank transfer; the transfer}

\label{lesson:ES-C628-transferencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to invest, then the Spanish for the cash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la transferencia}
\textbf{la transferencia} — \textquotedblleft{}the bank transfer; the transfer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Te hago una transferencia mañana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I will send you a bank transfer tomorrow.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Hacer una transferencia} — to make a transfer.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{transferencia} is a learned word built on Latin \emph{transferre} 'to carry across', from \emph{trans} and \emph{ferre} 'to carry' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la transferencia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la transferencia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la transferencia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to invest, then the Spanish for the cash, then say \emph{la transferencia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la transferencia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The bank transfer; the transfer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la hipoteca]{la hipoteca — the mortgage}

\label{lesson:ES-C628-hipoteca}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the cash, then the Spanish for the bank transfer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la hipoteca}
\textbf{la hipoteca} — \textquotedblleft{}the mortgage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pagamos la hipoteca cada mes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We pay the mortgage every month.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Hipotecar} — to mortgage.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hipoteca} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{hypotheca}, taken from Greek \emph{hypothēkē} 'a pledge, a deposit', built from \emph{hypo} 'under' and \emph{thēkē} 'a place to put things' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la hipoteca}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la hipoteca}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la hipoteca}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the cash, then the Spanish for the bank transfer, then say \emph{la hipoteca} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la hipoteca mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The mortgage\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el interés]{el interés — the interest}

\label{lesson:ES-C628-interes}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the bank transfer, then the Spanish for the mortgage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el interés}
\textbf{el interés} — \textquotedblleft{}the interest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El banco cobra un interés alto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The bank charges high interest.}
\end{quote}

Also interest in a subject: \emph{tengo interés en la historia}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{interés} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{interesse} 'to be between, to make a difference', built from \emph{inter} and \emph{esse} 'to be' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the bank transfer, then the Spanish for the mortgage, then say \emph{el interés} again

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[retirar]{retirar — to withdraw, to take out; to remove}

\label{lesson:ES-C628-retirar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the mortgage, then the Spanish for the interest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: retirar}
\textbf{retirar} — \textquotedblleft{}to withdraw, to take out; to remove\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Retiro dinero del cajero.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I take money out of the cash machine.}
\end{quote}

In speech people often say \emph{sacar dinero}. \emph{Retirarse} — to retire, to withdraw.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{retirar} is built on \emph{tirar} 'to pull, to throw' with \emph{re-}; \emph{tirar} is usually traced to a Germanic verb meaning 'to tear' (EtymDB), but its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{retirar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{retirar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{retirar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the mortgage, then the Spanish for the interest, then say \emph{retirar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
